mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.2% indicates an accommodative monetary policy environment that reduces the cost of capital for equity financing, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 7.0% signals economic distress that triggers central bank intervention, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 7.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105 and housing starts (HOUST) fall below 600, it indicates a sharp contraction in the real economy that prompts aggressive monetary and fiscal stimulus, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 105 and HOUST < 600.

mechanism_narrative: In the high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 7.0%), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive 20-day returns due to the expectation of aggressive monetary and fiscal stimulus.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 7.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level above 600 (thousands) indicates robust consumer demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and stimulates equity investment, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST > 600.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.0% signals restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates for equity valuation, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) falls below 136,000 thousand and retail sales (RSAFS) fall below 345,000 million, it indicates a contraction in consumer spending that prompts aggressive policy responses, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS < 136000 and RSAFS < 345000.

mechanism_narrative: A current industrial production level above 105 indicates strong manufacturing activity, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO > 105.
